# Jobs — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

Listings here are job vacancies and work/freelance offers, not physical items. Photos are often logos, posters, or portfolio shots — that is normal here. This category is the most scam-prone space in Nepali classifieds (fake recruitment, advance-fee fraud, overseas manpower cons): caution is the default, and publish only when the posting is unusually clearly legitimate — named employer or named skill/service, real location, plausible pay.

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other: typically around 550, most listings 350–15,000 (6 listings) — data is very thin; lean on general judgment.
The price field is unreliable in Jobs: it mixes monthly salaries (10,000–20,000), freelance rates (300–1,500), and placeholders. Never hold on price alone; instead, promised pay far above market for the role (e.g. lakhs per month for unskilled or overseas work) is a classic recruitment-scam signal -> hold.

## What good listings look like
- "🎨 Thumbnail Designer | Click-Worthy & Engaging Designs"
- "👉 Video Editor | Turning Ideas Into Content"
- "sales marketing" (price 20,000 = monthly salary for a local vacancy)
- "we will make crochet items as U want tops bags clips boquet just remember us"
A good listing names the specific role or skill, who is hiring (or offering the service), location or remote, and a salary/rate that fits the role. Most legitimate posts here are freelance/service offers or small local vacancies.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Overseas/manpower recruitment (Gulf, Malaysia, Japan, Korea, Europe visa or work offers) -> hold unless a named, licensed manpower agency with verifiable details is stated; any upfront fee to apply ("registration", "medical", "processing", "training" charge) is the core advance-fee fraud pattern.
- Vague high-pay offers with no employer, duties, or location — "work from home, earn 50,000/month", online typing/liking/investment tasks -> hold.
- "Ladies staff urgent"-style posts with no company name or role description are a known exploitative-recruitment bait pattern -> hold.
- Obvious physical goods posted under Jobs are common (live samples include a phone "honor400lite", "cycle", "power bank", "photo frame", "kushan cover", the sweet "Manbhavan(sonpapdi)") -> wrong category, hold.
